req.title: Login required for update
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-013 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who attempt GET /<id>/update are redirected to /auth/login. The violation was test[4]: kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is a structural/positive heuristic; a negative test exercising a state transition should use NEG or DT. Fix: change test[4] kind from 'negative' to 'positive' since the state-transition test verifies the correct system behaviour (redirect after logout) which is a positive scenario exercised via state transitions. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with seed data (post id=1 exists, author_id=5)
actions: Send GET /1/update without any session cookie
trace: R-FLASKR-013: anonymous GET /<id>/update must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/1/update')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_authenticated_user_get_update_returns_200
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with seed data (post id=2, author_id=1, user Rahul/stone)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: Send GET /2/update with the authenticated session
trace: R-FLASKR-013: authenticated users must NOT be redirected; they reach the update page
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302
r = client.get('/2/update')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.headers.get('Location') != '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_state_transition_logout_then_get_update_redirects
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Rahul logs in, then logs out
trace: R-FLASKR-013: state transition from authenticated to anonymous must re-trigger redirect
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302
r_auth = client.get('/2/update')
assert r_auth.status_code == 200
client.get('/auth/logout')
r_anon = client.get('/2/update')
assert r_anon.status_code == 302
assert r_anon.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_multiple_post_ids_all_redirect
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with seed data (posts 1..20 exist)
trace: R-FLASKR-013: redirect applies for all post IDs — boundary min/max coverage
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
for post_id in [1, 2, 20]:
    r = client.get(f'/{post_id}/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for post {post_id}, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Wrong Location for post {post_id}'
